question: After the general grammar repair reduced non-clBLAS errors to 13/386, does a clBLAS template prepass meet G-R6's separate two-independent-project convention guard?
convention_tested: A .cl file that is a C host string declaration (static const char *name = followed by an unescaped multiline quote), containing OpenCL kernel text and percent substitution tokens such as %TYPE, %PREFIX and %PTYPE; a host generator consumes that template. A different mechanism for embedding or generating kernels does not count as the same convention.
interpretation: Authenticated repository-wide code searches found only the admitted clBLAS source and three clBLAS-derived template trees. Four scoped candidates returned zero exact-token hits. The three global exact-token queries returned 32, 92 and 92 file hits across the same four numeric repository IDs. Twenty-five template paths per repository match the pinned clBLAS tree; exact blob matches are 25, 25, 25 and 22, with three modified blobs in the last tree. Copies of the same library are not a second independent convention implementation. This is bounded indexed-query evidence, not proof that no unindexed or differently expressed convention exists. G-R6 still authorizes no prepass; runtime product behavior and a second independent project remain unmet.
request_method: Authenticated public HTTPS GET with existing GitHub credentials held in memory, Accept application/vnd.github+json and API version 2022-11-28. Raw responses were saved privately with exclusive file creation. Searches used per_page=100, page=1; every total_count was <=100, item_count matched, incomplete_results=false and all results were public. Code requests were spaced by at least 6.3 seconds. sha256 values hash exact response bytes, with no reserialization.
publication_policy: X-R9: non-subject repository identities are numeric IDs only. Account names, slugs, scoped query URLs and source paths remain private. The admitted clBLAS subject retains its public pin.
